<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Part&nbsp;I.</font></b><a name="Parti__083727"></a></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 1.&#160; <i>BUSINESS.</i></font></b><a name="Item1_Business__083728"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">GENERAL</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alteva,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; was incorporated in New York on January&nbsp;16, 1902 and is qualified to do business as a foreign corporation in various states. Unless otherwise indicated or unless the context requires otherwise, all references in this Annual Report to the &#147;Company,&#148; &#147;we,&#148; &#147;our&#148; or &#147;us,&#148; means Alteva,&nbsp;Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries.&#160; Our executive offices are located at 401 Market Street, First Floor, Philadelphia, PA&#160; 19106 and our telephone number is 877-258-3722.&#160; We also maintain another office in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania and an office in Warwick, New York.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Annual Reports on Form&nbsp;10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form&nbsp;10-Q, and Current Reports on Form&nbsp;8-K, and any amendments thereto, are available free of charge on our website at www.Alteva.com under the &#147;Investors&#148; tab as soon as reasonably practical after filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#147;SEC&#148;).&#160; This website address is for information only and is not intended to be an active link or to incorporate any website information into this document.&#160; In addition, our reports filed with the SEC may be read at the public reference facility maintained by the SEC at its public reference room at 100 F. <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are a premier provider of hosted Unified Communications as a Service (&#147;UCaaS&#148;) that significantly enhances business productivity and efficiency.&#160; Our UCaaS solution integrates and optimizes best-in-class cloud-based technologies and business applications to deliver a comprehensive voice, video and collaboration service for the office and mobile workforce.&#160; We are committed to delivering meaningful value to our customers through a consistent, high quality and unified user experience across multiple devices, platforms and operating systems.&#160; These attributes have positioned us as a leading hosted communications provider and the partner of choice for a growing number of business customers nationwide and internationally.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our cloud-based Unified Communications (&#147;UC&#148;) solutions are focused on serving the needs of small, medium, large and enterprise businesses that require the highest quality voice and integrated business productivity applications. We design and integrate our customers&#146; unique communication needs for multi-location offices, remote workers, mobile workers, customer relationship management (&#147;CRM&#148;) applications like Salesforce.com, business productivity tools and analytics, into a single seamless experience. We also design customized solutions for specialized vertical market requirements to optimize our services alongside critical business operations. These vertical markets include legal, healthcare, finance, retail and more.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2011, we purchased substantially all of the assets and assumed certain liabilities of Alteva, LLC, a cloud-based UC solutions provider and a leading provider of enterprise hosted Voice over Internet Protocol (&#147;VoIP&#148;) in North America.</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; This acquisition was a significant part of our strategy to become a leading provider of world-class UC solutions. As part of our efforts to further improve performance of the UC segment, we restructured our business by exiting, effective September&nbsp;1, 2013, our Syracuse, New York operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also operate as a regional Incumbent Local Exchange Carrier </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(&#147;ILEC&#148;) in southern Orange County, New York and northern New Jersey.&#160; Our Telephone segment consists of providing local and toll telephone service, high-speed broadband Internet service, and satellite video service to residential and business customers.&#160; Our ILEC service areas are primarily rural and have an estimated population of 50,000.&#160; We also operate as a Competitive Local Exchange Carrier (&#147;CLEC&#148;) in areas that are adjacent to our ILEC territories and beyond.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Unified Communications</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alteva is a premier provider of hosted UCaaS that significantly enhances business productivity and efficiency. Alteva&#146;s UCaaS solution integrates and optimizes best-in-class cloud-based technologies and business applications to deliver a comprehensive voice, video and collaboration service for the multi-location office and mobile workforce.&#160; Alteva is committed to delivering meaningful value to our customers through a consistent, high quality and unified user experience across multiple devices, platforms and operating systems.&#160; These attributes have positioned Alteva as a leading hosted communications provider and the partner of choice for a growing number of business customers nationwide and internationally.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At Alteva, we aim to be the most trusted provider of knowledge, services and tools that simplify communications and enable business efficiency. We are driven by a pursuit of excellence and strive to be world-class in everything we do. Through our core characteristics of enthusiasm, commitment, perseverance and leadership, we are dedicated to providing our customers with excellent service. This includes both the technology itself and the support infrastructure surrounding it. As a part of this effort, we are excited to deliver the most innovative communications technologies available on the market, in the easiest way possible.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alteva has always prided itself on being at the forefront of our industry and we constantly push to improve our product capabilities, platform reliability and customer support services. Again, 2014 was no exception as evidenced by the enhancements to the business user experience, including advanced upgrades to the integration of our hosted voice services with productivity tools like Google Apps for Business and Microsoft Office, CRM applications like Salesforce.com and Clio for legal practice management.&#160; Additionally we continued to enhance many of our products including, video-enabled devices, enhanced SIP trunking capabilities, advanced call center technologies, Microsoft Lync messaging solutions, and workforce mobility solutions across smartphone and desktop platforms including Windows, Apple Mac, iOS and Android devices.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alteva continually strives to be an innovator and leader in the marketplace.&#160; Our UC service tightly integrates business productivity applications, collaboration tools and multiple communication devices (desk phones, smart phones, laptops and tablets), into a single solution with advanced capabilities such as data analytics.&#160; Our best-in-class products have been recognized numerous times, including most recently in 2014 with awards such as the Lync Pioneer Award,&nbsp;Internet Telephony Excellence Award from Internet Telephony Magazine and the Communications Solutions Product of the Year Award for Alteva Mobility from TMC, a global, integrated media company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alteva&#146;s UC solution integrates Hosted VoIP with business productivity applications including Microsoft Office, Google Apps for Business, Salesforce and vertical market specific software, and allows for a truly cloud-based UC environment where basic business technologies like voice communications, instant messaging, video conferencing, desktop sharing and more, are fully integrated with each user&#146;s productivity software of choice.&#160; Alteva provides a reliable, flexible and fully scalable telecommunications solution for enterprise businesses and call centers and enhances an organization&#146;s communications strategy by offering mobility, flexibility, scalability and redundancy, while reducing the total cost of ownership (&#147;TCO&#148;).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alteva&#146;s communications infrastructure is a uniquely integrated platform including typical UC components, such as voice, video, instant messaging and presence blended with specialized applications such as mobile integration, VoIP dial tone replacement for premise based private branch exchange systems (&#147;PBX&#148;), email, call center solutions, call recording, call data analytics, and CRM software integration.&#160; We have enhanced our product development process to speed-up time-to-market for new products and services that meet identified end-user needs.&#160; This process is designed to consistently improve the end-user experience and bring increased value to our customers through UC services.&#160; The process starts by identifying a market opportunity, capturing detailed market requirements and performing business analysis.&#160; Subsequent to this, working groups from the relevant functional areas of the Company come together to rapidly develop and deploy each new solution.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to offering a comprehensive solution for businesses, Alteva offers for white-label resale its voice, video and data solutions which can be integrated with the wholesale customer&#146;s existing product portfolio.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alteva&#146;s services are provided through our world-class BroadSoft and telecommunications infrastructure, allowing us to provide a level of service and support typically only available through the largest (Tier 1) service providers.&#160; Our geographically redundant infrastructure enables our platform to provide continuous operations to our customers, even during a catastrophic event, such as hurricanes and other unforeseen disasters.</font></p>

The functionality of these platforms enables our network to be flexible to every customer&#146;s needs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Class&nbsp;5 BroadSoft cloud-based platform enables geographic redundancy, advanced PBX functionality and is highly scalable enabling the network to support businesses from 1 to 100,000+ users and scales to millions of total subscribers.&#160; The Class&nbsp;4 carrier platform is Alteva&#146;s carrier infrastructure and includes components from AcmePacket and Genband. This enables geographic redundancy in addition to interconnectivity with over seven major carriers which are managed using an enhanced routing engine from TransNexus. This allows Alteva to have a more comprehensive footprint both domestic and internationally.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Network Operations Center (&#147;NOC&#148;) continually monitors various aspects of our network including: customer connectivity, customer premise equipment (&#147;CPE&#148;) and our call processing infrastructure. There are monitoring systems in place for our specialized voice firewalls and hosted Class&nbsp;5 PBX feature servers. In addition we also use key performance indicators for the networks, servers and infrastructure and have customized fraud/denial of service management systems.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Telephone</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alteva operates as an ILEC in southern Orange County, New York and northern New Jersey.&#160; Our Telephone segment consists of providing local and toll telephone service, high-speed broadband and fiber Internet access services and satellite video services to residential and business customers.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ILEC service areas are primarily rural and have an estimated population of 50,000.&#160; We also operate as a CLEC in in Middletown, New York, Scotchtown, New York and Franklin Borough, New Jersey.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Services and Products</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Local network services &#151; Local network services include traditional dial tone that is primarily used to make or to receive voice, fax or analog modem calls from a residence or business.&#160; Our local network services are regulated by the Federal Communication Commission (&#147;FCC&#148;), New York Public Service Corporation (&#147;NYPSC&#148;) and the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (&#147;NJBPU&#148;).&#160; Included under local network services are custom calling services such as caller ID, call waiting, voice mail and other value-added services.&#160; These features allow users to display the number and/or name of callers, signal to the telephone user that additional calls are coming in, and send and receive voice messages.&#160; The sale of telephone and other equipment does not constitute a material part of our business.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Internet &#151; Broadband Internet and dial-up Internet access services are provided using our network and by reselling other suppliers&#146; access services.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">TV &#151;TV service enables us to bundle voice, TV and data, known as the &#147;Triple Play,&#148; to our customers.&#160; We have a reseller agreement with DIRECTV&#174; that allows us to provide the TV component of the Triple Play.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Network access services &#151; Network access services connect a customer&#146;s telephone or other equipment to the transmission facilities of other carriers that provide long distance and other communications services.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long distance services &#151; Long distance services result from the transport of intraLATA telecommunications traffic (traffic within our Local Access and Transport Area) to a destination that is outside of a local calling area.&#160; We also provide wire line interLATA long distance (commonly known as traditional long distance service) to our customers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Directory services </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#151; Our directory service group publishes and sells yellow and white page&nbsp;advertising in both print and online.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Other services and sales </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#151; These services relate primarily to billing and collections provided to other carriers, inside wire revenue, circuit revenue, wireless services, and reciprocal compensation.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Within the Telephone segment, we resell toll telephone services to our subscribers.&#160; We operate in an extremely competitive marketplace with other interexchange carriers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We began operating as a competitive local exchange carrier or CLEC in Middletown, New York in 1999, in Scotchtown, New York in 2001 and Franklin Borough, New Jersey in 2002.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Orange County-Poughkeepsie Limited Partnership</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We were a limited partner in the Orange County-Poughkeepsie Limited Partnership (&#147;O-P&#148;) and had an 8.108% limited partnership interest in the O-P until April&nbsp;30, 2014, which was accounted for under the equity method of accounting.&nbsp; The majority owner and general partner of the O-P is Verizon Wireless of the East LP (&#147;Verizon&#148;).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;26, 2011, we entered into an agreement (the &#147;4G Agreement&#148;) with Verizon and Cellco Partnership (d/b/a Verizon Wireless), the other limited partner, in the O-P to make certain changes to the O-P partnership agreement which, among other things, specifies that the O-P will provide 4G cellular services.&nbsp; The 4G Agreement provides that the O-P&#146;s business will be converted from a wholesale business to a retail business.&nbsp; In addition, the 4G Agreement provided for guaranteed annual cash distributions to us from the O-P through 2013.&nbsp; For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, we received annual cash distributions from the O-P of $13.0 million.&nbsp; Starting in 2014, the 4G Agreement provided that we would receive cash distributions equal to our ownership share percentage of the approved total distributions by the O-P. The 4G Agreement also gave us the right (the &#147;Put&#148;) to require Verizon to purchase all of our ownership interest in the O-P</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Major Customers</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">COMPETITION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Unified Communications</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a hosted UC provider, Alteva competes with both premise-based voice and video providers such as Avaya and Cisco as well as cloud-based voice and UC providers such as&nbsp;8x8,&nbsp;Inc., Verizon and Comcast. As the market expands, there is an increasing number of services providers and competitors. The competitive landscape for hosted UC includes traditional telephone providers, managed service providers, system integrators, as well as non-traditional competitors.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alteva continues to be recognized as an industry leader in UC services.&#160; Alteva has differentiated itself by delivering a best-in-class product portfolio, supported by industry leading implementation and customer service that cannot be easily matched by our competitors, large or small.&#160; In order to continue to create a competitive advantage and establish differentiation in the hosted UC market place, Alteva expects to adapt and remain on the forefront of technology, creating a position among the most stable and respected communications vendors around the globe.&#160; Alteva integrates new innovations with proven technology from industry leaders like Microsoft, Cisco, BroadSoft, Level 3, and Polycom to provide best-in-class hosted UC solutions.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Telephone</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Telecommunications Act of 1996 (the &#147;1996 Act&#148;) created a nationwide structure in which competition is allowed and encouraged between ILECs, interexchange carriers, competitive access providers, cable TV companies and other entities.&#160; Our local network, network access and long distance services compete with large cellular telephone providers, cable companies and VoIP providers that offer alternative voice products.&#160; These competitors, in many cases, are much larger and have greater resources and previously had greater regulatory flexibility than us.&#160; During the last several years, we have experienced overall declines in telephone access lines as customers have migrated towards cellular and VoIP providers for telephone services in our regulated franchise area.&#160; We primarily compete on the basis of price, convenience, call quality and reliability for telephone services.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our broadband Internet and dial-up Internet services primarily compete with Cablevision in New York and Service Electric in New Jersey.&#160; These cable companies are much larger and have greater resources and regulatory flexibility than us.&#160; The present market environment requires that we compete on the basis of service, speed and price.&#160; Whether customer and pricing levels can be maintained depends, in part, on the actions of existing competitors, the possible entry into the market of new competitors, the rate of technological change and the evolving level of demand for voice, video and high-speed data services.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our TV service competes against entrenched cable companies and satellite television companies.&#160; To stay competitive in the current market environment we must be able to offer a television service on par with our competitors at a competitive price.&#160; Accordingly, we offer TV services provided by DIRECTV&#174;, which enables us to offer our Triple Play bundle.&#160; However, the success of our Triple Play offering has been limited by competing offerings by Cablevision in New York and Service Electric in New Jersey.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also provide directory services in our telephone segment.&#160; Our directory services compete with other online providers of directory</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">7<a name="PB_7_081949_7748"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">listings as well as in market competitors of print services, such as Yellow Book, Verizon, Frontier, and CenturyLink.&#160; We primarily compete on the basis of price, our local presence and our loyal customer base that use our directory listings.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ILEC service areas are surrounded by competitive telephone companies located within a 30-mile radius of Warwick, New York.&#160; For voice, video and data services, we compete with Cablevision in our New York serving area and Service Electric in our New Jersey serving area.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We currently compete for local service (access lines) with ILECs in the Middletown, New York area, as well as the Franklin Borough, New Jersey area.&#160; The local exchange carriers in these markets are larger and have greater resources than us.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">REGULATION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The communications industry has been and remains the subject of significant legislative and regulatory oversight at both federal and state levels.&#160; The 1996 Act, which updated the Communications Act of 1934, provided a structure for local competition. The implementation of the 1996 Act requires interpretation by the Federal Communications Commission (&#147;FCC&#148;), states and courts.&#160; Congress also frequently proposes legislative amendments to the 1996 Act.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 1996 Act opened local telecommunications markets to competition, preempting state and local laws to the extent that they prevented competitive entry into a market.&#160; The 1996 Act allows states to retain the authority to preserve universal service, protect public safety and welfare, ensure quality of service, protect consumers and mediate and arbitrate disputes involving interconnection agreements between carriers.&#160; The 1996 Act generally requires local carriers to interconnect with other carriers, unbundle their services at wholesale rates, permit resale of their services, enable collocation of equipment, provide Local Number Portability (&#147;LNP&#148;) and dialing parity, provide access to poles, ducts, conduits and rights-of-way, and complete calls originating by competing carriers under termination agreements.&#160; To respond to the 1996 Act&#146;s requirements, we entered into interconnection agreements with other carriers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We serve as an ILEC, a CLEC and as a broadband service provider.&#160; As such, we are subject to both state and federal regulation.&#160; We pursue regulatory and legislative policies that will further diminish regulatory burdens imposed on us.&#160; However, as an ILEC, we remain subject to more regulation than our competitors.&#160; The following summary of the regulatory environment in which our business operates does not describe all present and proposed federal and state regulations affecting the communications industry.&#160; These laws and regulations are subject to change and any change may have an adverse effect on us in the future.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Federal Regulation</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interstate toll and access service revenues are subject to the jurisdiction of the FCC.&#160; We receive reimbursement from carriers in the form of charges for providing carriers with access to and from our local network in addition to the compensation we receive from providing services to our end user customers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As an ILEC, we are subject to regulation that is generally more extensive than the regulation of our competitors for certain services.&#160; This regulation covers our rates and service terms, and also affects the terms on which we must provide connections and network elements to competitors.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In contrast, wireless service providers are not regulated from a retail-pricing standpoint, but are subject to various licensing and technical requirements imposed by the FCC, including provisions related to the acquisition, assignment or transfer of radio licenses.&#160; Wireless service providers are also subject to mandates, such as enhanced 911, or E-911, and wireless LNP.&#160; Long distance and wireless service providers, which compete against us and are also our wholesale customers, are less regulated, without significant rate regulations or tariffing obligations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cable operators offering local and long distance voice services face less regulation of these services than we face as an ILEC. A small but growing category of VoIP providers offer services that compete with our wire line offerings and also face a lighter regulatory burden.&#160; The FCC has preempted states from exercising entry and related economic regulation of such VoIP providers but the FCC has not preempted state regulation of fixed VoIP service commonly offered by cable operators.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The advent of VoIP services being provided by cable television and other companies has heightened the need for federal and state regulators to determine whether VoIP is subject to the same regulatory and financial constraints as wire line telephone service.&#160; On November&nbsp;9, 2004, the FCC issued an order in response to a petition from Vonage declaring that Vonage-style VoIP services were exempt from state telecommunications regulations. The FCC order applies to all VoIP offerings provided over broadband services. However, this order did not clarify; whether or under what terms VoIP traffic may be subject to intercarrier compensation requirements; whether VoIP was subject to state tax or commercial business regulations; or whether VoIP providers had to comply with obligations related to 911 emergency calls, the USF and the Communications Assistance for Law Enforcement Act (&#147;CALEA&#148;).&#160; The FCC addressed these issues through its &#147;IP-Enabled Services Proceedings,&#148; which opened in February&nbsp;2004.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June&nbsp;3, 2005, the FCC issued an order establishing rules&nbsp;requiring VoIP service providers to incorporate 911 emergency call capabilities for their customers as a standard feature of their services, rather than an optional enhancement.&#160; On September&nbsp;23, 2005, the FCC required interconnected VoIP and broadband Internet access service providers to comply with CALEA by mid-2007.&#160; In 2006, the FCC began the assessment of USF charges on VoIP providers.&#160; On October&nbsp;31, 2007, Congress enacted the Internet Tax Freedom Act Amendments Act which established that state and local authorities could tax VoIP services.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8<a name="PB_8_082014_141"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
</div>
<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='8',FILE='C:\JMS\C901917\15-1883-1\task7276916\1883-1-bi.htm',USER='C901917',CD='Mar 16 17:53 2015' -->

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other issues regarding VoIP, such as classification, treatment, and funding continue to be a subject of FCC scrutiny. These issues continue to generate interest within the industry as they can affect ILEC charges for terminating VoIP calls and competitive parity among services and service providers. We cannot be certain whether and when the FCC will further clarify or modify rules&nbsp;governing treatment of VoIP services, or how any rule&nbsp;changes may ultimately affect us.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">One of our telephone subsidiaries offer services as an Internet Service Provider (&#147;ISP&#148;).</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Federal government authorities, including the FCC and the U.S. Congress, have considered proposals to regulate ISPs and network operators regarding the management of their networks and the use of information about their subscribers.&#160; The decision by a federal appeals court in January, 2014 was that the FCC had effectively over reached in the rules&nbsp;it had written to assure net neutrality for broadband.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;26, 2015, the FCC announced that it had voted to apply Communications Act Title II regulation to the Internet.&#160; This is a major policy change, and would bring the Internet under traditional utility regulation.&#160; The FCC has in the past treated broadband services as lightly regulated or unregulated Title I services under the Communications Act.&#160; The new rules&nbsp;will apply to both wired and mobile broadband networks and services.&#160; The FCC rules&nbsp;have three specific requirements:&#160; (1)&nbsp;No Blocking: broadband providers may not block access to legal content, applications, services, or non-harmful devices; (2)&nbsp;No Throttling: broadband providers may not impair or degrade lawful Internet traffic on the basis of content, applications, services, or non-harmful devices; and (3)&nbsp;No Paid Prioritization: broadband providers may not favor some lawful Internet traffic over other lawful traffic in exchange for consideration &#151; in other words, no &#147;fast lanes.&#148; This rule&nbsp;also bans ISPs from prioritizing content and services of their affiliates.&#160; The rules&nbsp;also contain a general Open Internet conduct standard requiring that ISPs cannot harm consumers or edge providers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Congress requires the FCC to refrain (&#147;forbear&#148;) from enforcing provisions of the Communications Act that are not in the public interest. The FCC rules&nbsp;will apply some key provisions of Title II, and forbear from applying others.&#160; The major provisions of Title II which the rules&nbsp;will apply include:&#160; (1)&nbsp;&#147;core&#148; provisions of Title II: Sections 201 and 202 (prohibiting, among other things, &#147;unjust and unreasonable practices&#148;); (2)&nbsp;investigation of consumer complaints under section 208 and related enforcement provisions, specifically sections 206, 207, 209, 216 and 217; (3)&nbsp;consumer privacy under Section&nbsp;222; (4)&nbsp;access to poles and conduits under Section&nbsp;224; (5)&nbsp; people with disabilities under Sections 225 and 255; and (5)&nbsp;universal service fund support for broadband service in the future through partial application of Section&nbsp;254.&#160; The major provisions of Title II which the rules&nbsp;will not apply (under forbearance) include:&#160; (1)&nbsp;any requirement concerning tariffs or other forms of rate approval, unbundling, or other forms of utility regulation; (2)&nbsp;mandatory contributions to the Universal Service Fund under Section&nbsp;254; and (3)&nbsp;any imposition of new taxes or fees.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The new FCC rules&nbsp;have yet to be published officially, and are almost certain to cause major litigation by affected parties.&#160; Several parties, including broadband network and service providers, have claimed that the new rules&nbsp;are unnecessary</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and will inhibit investment.&#160; The new rules&nbsp;will take full effect unless either the FCC or a federal court issues a stay of the rules&nbsp;pending full adjudication of all judicial challenges.&#160; The litigation over these rules&nbsp;could take several years before final resolution.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At this stage, we cannot predict to what extent these new rules&nbsp;will allow us greater flexibility to manage our network or charge content providers.&#160; Nor can we predict whether other regulations or legislation concerning Internet services will be adopted that may increase costs, reduce potential revenues, or create regulatory disadvantages.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">State Regulation</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The New York telephone service operations offered by our subsidiary, Alteva of Warwick LLC, are subject to the jurisdiction of the NYPSC and our New Jersey telephone service operations are subject to the jurisdiction of the NJBPU.&#160; These two bodies have regulatory authority over Alteva of Warwick LLC&#146;s local exchange operations with respect to rates, facilities, services, reports, and other matters.&#160; As a result, Alteva of Warwick&#146;s ability to respond quickly to changing market conditions or to implement a new business organization can be limited by the necessity of obtaining regulatory reviews or responding to interrogatories which can slow down or even prevent the desired transaction.&#160; As an ILEC, Alteva of Warwick LLC, generally faces carrier of last resort, or COLR, obligations which include an ongoing requirement to provide service to all prospective and current customers in Alteva of Warwick LLC&#146;s service territories who request service and are willing to pay rates prescribed in Alteva of Warwick&#146;s tariffs.&#160; In competitively bid situations, such as newly constructed housing developments or multi-tenant dwellings, this may constitute a competitive disadvantage to Alteva of Warwick if competitors can choose to exclusively tie service to homeowner&#146;s association fees or choose not to provide service to customers who are poor credit risks or customers they believe it would not be economically viable to serve.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Intrastate billing and collection services remain partly regulated in New York. The regulated services are provided under tariff.&#160; Some carriers provide their own billing and collection services and do not use Alteva of Warwick&#146;s services.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alteva of Warwick LLC, along with other carriers, has been granted pricing flexibility under a March&nbsp;4, 2008 NYPSC ruling for various intrastate retail telecommunications services.&#160; We have taken advantage of this flexibility to raise our rates for these services in all subsequent years.&#160; Alteva of Warwick LLC anticipates having the option to apply for further increases.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Federal Universal Service Fund</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">USF programs provide funding for services in high-cost areas; funding for reduced-rate services to low-income consumers; and funding for discounted communications and Internet access services for schools, libraries and rural health care facilities.&#160; These programs are funded by contributions from telecommunications carriers and VoIP providers who are interconnected to the network.&#160; These contributions are based on an FCC-prescribed percentage and are recovered from customers through surcharges.&#160; In September&nbsp;2005, the FCC</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">9<a name="PB_9_082044_7608"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
</div>
<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='9',FILE='C:\JMS\C901917\15-1883-1\task7276916\1883-1-bi.htm',USER='C901917',CD='Mar 16 17:53 2015' -->

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">deregulated ILECs&#146; high-speed Internet access service and in the process eliminated the universal service assessments on end users of such services.&#160; Universal service assessments on the wholesale provision of such services, however, remain in place.&#160; In June&nbsp;2006, the FCC required certain VoIP providers to contribute to the USF.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;28, 2011, the FCC released a comprehensive order regarding reform of the USF and Intercarrier Compensation (&#147;ICC&#148;).&#160;&#160; The order specified that the USF would be renamed the Connect America Fund (&#147;CAF&#148;).&#160; Funds from CAF will be allocated with a greater emphasis on stimulating broadband build out in the United States.&#160; Additionally, this order mandated the decline in overall revenues deemed interstate.&#160; Currently these revenues are received from end users,&nbsp;Interexchange carriers and the USF. The total of these revenues will decline 5% a year and the USF or CAF support must adjust accordingly.&#160; This change commenced July&nbsp;1, 2012 and will continue annually for the next 10 years.&#160; Finally, the order contains a provision that implements a &#147;ceiling&#148; on the amount of corporate overhead expenses that can be recovered by an ILEC through the CAF. Historically the USF fund has allowed ILECs to recover their reasonable costs without restriction.&#160; In 2012 a ceiling was established based on corporate overhead cost per access line.&#160; Accordingly, we have experienced a reduction in funds we are eligible to receive from the CAF.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to FCC requirements mentioned above, we contribute to the USF/CAF.&nbsp; Our obligation to this fund was $1.0 million and $1.3 million, in 2014 and 2013, respectively.&nbsp; The Universal Service Administration Company (&#147;USAC&#148;) establishes a contribution rate for eligible revenues which in turn determines the amount of the annual obligation to the fund.&nbsp; Future contribution levels&nbsp;will therefore depend&nbsp;on revenues and USAC mandated&nbsp;contribution rates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have been designated as an Eligible Telecommunications Carrier (&#147;ETC&#148;) in New York and New Jersey, which has enabled us, since January&nbsp;1, 1998, to receive substantial USF monies from USAC.&#160; As a result of FCC orders, all local exchange carriers have been required to reduce interstate access charges billed to toll carriers.&#160; To offset this revenue reduction, monthly payments from the high cost portion of the USF are provided to carriers with ETC status and other requirements set forth in the orders.&#160; We meet these requirements.&#160; As a further assurance of stability of cost recovery, we elected to participate in the Tariff/Pool administrated by National Exchange Carrier Association,&nbsp;Inc. (NECA) effective July&nbsp;1, 2006.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">USF/CAF revenue and NECA pool settlements, (&#147;regulatory revenue&#148;) accounted for $0.8 million and $1.4 million, in 2014 and 2013, respectively.&#160; This is included in operating revenue in our consolidated statements of operations.&#160; Regulatory revenue is subject to change based upon many factors, including regulatory changes, our performance, and the performance of other companies that receive regulatory revenue.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Intercarrier Compensation</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Intercarrier compensation includes regulated interstate and intrastate switched access charges and also reciprocal compensation received by ILECs, CLECs and wireless service providers.&#160; This compensation is received from long distance carriers to pay for the origination and termination of long distance calls and from interconnected local carriers to pay for terminating local and wireless calls. On average, intrastate switched access charges, which are currently regulated by state Public Utility Commissions, are generally higher than interstate switched access charges, which are regulated by the FCC, and in turn interstate switched access charges are generally higher on a per-minute basis than are reciprocal compensation rates. In February&nbsp;2010, the NJBPU ordered the intrastate switched access terminating rates for New Jersey to be transitioned to the lower interstate rates over a two-year period.&#160; We fully transitioned to meet this requirement in 2012. The NYPSC ordered that New York intrastate terminating rates must match interstate rates on July&nbsp;1, 2013. We fully met this requirement in 2013.&#160;&#160; NYPSC is also considering changes to intrastate originating rates in a current docket.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As mentioned above, on November&nbsp;28, 2011, the FCC released a comprehensive order which also concerned intercarrier compensation.&#160; The order reflected the FCC&#146;s desire that telephone companies eventually eliminate intercarrier switched access compensation altogether. To implement this, the FCC mandated that companies lower their terminating access rates at the intrastate level to the interstate rate level by 2013 (see above). In addition, a rate of return carrier like us must reduce our rates for some access elements to zero in nine years.&#160; While this will be offset to some extent by additional end user charges (known as ARC or Access Recovery Charge). The overall effect will be a decline in revenue.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The order also clarified that VOIP traffic must pay access charges which went into effect on July&nbsp;1, 2012.&#160; Finally, under the order, reciprocal compensation charges for wireless carriers on Intra MTA traffic was eliminated on July&nbsp;1, 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">EMPLOYEES</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of February&nbsp;27, 2015, we had 109 full-time and 4 part-time employees, including 27 non-management employees represented by Local 503 of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers.&#160; The existing contract with our union employees expires on October&nbsp;31, 2016.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">EXECUTIVE OFFICERS OF THE REGISTRANT</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Information regarding our executive officers is presented below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 1A.&#160; <i>RISK FACTORS.</i></font></b><a name="Item1a_RiskFactors__083750"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">RISK FACTORS</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">We have a history of operating losses and there is no assurance we will generate profits in the future.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have a history of operating losses.&#160; We have sustained operating losses of $6.6 million and </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$11.6 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively.&#160; We cannot assure that we will be able to generate profitable operations in the future.&#160; If we cannot generate profits in the future, our failure to do so could adversely affect the market price of our common stock, which in turn could adversely affect our ability to raise additional equity capital or to incur additional debt.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Any impairment of goodwill, other intangible assets or long-lived assets could negatively impact our results of operations.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our goodwill is subject to an impairment test on an annual basis and, along with other intangible assets or long-lived assets, is also tested whenever events and circumstances indicate that goodwill, intangible assets and/or long-lived assets may be impaired.&#160; Any excess goodwill, indefinite-lived intangible assets value resulting from the impairment test must be written off in the period of determination.&#160; Intangible assets (other than goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets) and other long-lived assets are generally amortized or depreciated over the useful life of such assets.&#160; In addition, from time to time, we may acquire or make an investment in a business that will require us to record goodwill based on the purchase price and the value of the acquired tangible and intangible assets.&#160; We significantly increased our goodwill as a result of our acquisition of substantially all of the assets and assumed certain liabilities of Alteva, LLC.&#160; We may subsequently experience unforeseen issues with the businesses we acquire, which may adversely affect the anticipated returns of the business or value of the intangible assets and trigger an evaluation of the recoverability of the recorded goodwill and intangible assets for such business.&#160; Likewise, our Telephone segment has continued to decline in revenue.&#160; Further declines in revenue could cause a future impairment of long-lived assets in the Telephone segment.&#160; Future determinations of significant write-offs of goodwill, intangible assets or other long-lived assets, as a result of an impairment test or any accelerated amortization or depreciation of other intangible assets or other long-lived assets could have a material negative impact on our results of operations and financial condition.&#160; We have completed our annual impairment test for goodwill in accordance with the applicable accounting guidance, and have concluded that we do not have any impairment of goodwill for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The UC market is also becoming increasingly competitive as large and small providers grow more sophisticated in their UC product offerings.&#160; We cannot predict the number of competitors that will ultimately emerge, but increased competition from existing and new entities could have an adverse effect on our business.&#160; In our Telephone segment, we historically faced little competition in our markets.&#160; As a direct result of deregulation, we now face direct competition in our traditional ILEC territories by CLEC operations and other providers of telecommunications services that offer comparable voice, video and data products.&#160; The primary competitor in our market has brand recognition and financial, personnel, marketing and other resources that are significantly greater than ours.&#160; In addition, consolidations and strategic alliances within the telecommunications industry, as well as ongoing technological innovation, are likely to increase competition in our market. With increased substitution of wireless for landline services, wireless carriers are now competing aggressively for our voice customers.</font></p>

We might not be able to successfully integrate future transactions into our business or operate the businesses profitably, and we may be subject to unanticipated problems and liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">If we cannot continue to license or enforce the intellectual property rights on which our business depends, or if third parties assert that we violate their intellectual property rights, then </font></i></b><b><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We rely upon patent, copyright, trademark and trade secret laws in the United States, and similar laws in other countries, and non-disclosure, confidentiality and other types of agreements with our employees, customers, suppliers and other parties, to establish, maintain and enforce our intellectual property rights.&#160; Despite these measures, any of our direct or indirect intellectual property rights could be challenged, invalidated, circumvented, infringed or misappropriated, or such intellectual property rights may not be sufficient to permit us to take advantage of current market trends or otherwise to provide competitive advantages, which could result in costly software redesign efforts, discontinuance of certain product offerings or other competitive harm.&#160; Further, the laws of certain countries do not protect proprietary rights to the same extent as the laws of the United States.&#160; Therefore, in certain jurisdictions, we may be unable to protect our proprietary technology adequately against unauthorized third party copying, infringement or use, which could adversely affect our competitive position.&#160; Also, because of the rapid pace of technological change in the telecommunications industry, much of our UC business and many of our UC products rely on key technologies developed or licensed by third parties, and we may not be able to obtain or continue to obtain licenses and technologies from these third parties at all or on reasonable terms.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Claims of intellectual property infringement also might require us to redesign affected products, enter into costly settlement or license agreements or pay costly damage awards, or face a temporary or permanent injunction prohibiting us from marketing or selling certain of our products.&#160; Even if we have an agreement to indemnify us against such costs, the indemnifying party may be unable to uphold its contractual obligations.&#160; If we cannot or do not license the infringed technology at all, license the technology on reasonable terms or substitute similar technology from another source, our revenue and earnings could be adversely impacted.&#160; Finally, we use open source software in connection with our products and services.&#160; Companies that incorporate open source software into their products have, from time to time, faced claims challenging the ownership of open source software and/or compliance with open source license terms.&#160; As a result, we could be subject to suits by parties claiming ownership of what we believe to be open source software or noncompliance with open source licensing terms.&#160; Some open source software licenses require users who distribute open source software as part of their software to publicly disclose all or part of the source code to such software and/or make available any derivative works of the open source code on unfavorable terms or at no cost.&#160; Any requirement to disclose our source code or pay damages for breach of contract could be harmful to our business results of operations and financial condition.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">We may not be able to successfully integrate new technologies, respond effectively to customer requirements or provide new services.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The communications industry is subject to rapid and significant changes in technology, the development of new types of content, frequent new service offerings and a changing regulatory and economic environment.&#160; We cannot predict the changes in our competitive position or profitability.&#160; Technological developments may reduce the competitiveness of our networks and require significant expenditures of capital to upgrade and/or replace outdated technologies.&#160; In addition, new products and services arising out of technological developments in the industry may reduce the attractiveness of our products and services.&#160; If we fail to adapt successfully to technological changes or obsolescence, or fail to obtain access to important new technologies or content, we could lose existing customers and fail to attract new customers.&#160; Our UC business currently depends on the use of desktop telephones and related systems.&#160; The rise of social media and soft phones in the future could potentially reduce the use of desktop telephones, which could have an adverse effect on our UC business.&#160; A key element of our long-term growth strategy is our ability to deliver new and enhanced products and services to our customers.&#160; The successful delivery of new products and services is uncertain and dependent on many factors.&#160; There is no guarantee that delivery of these services will generate the anticipated increase in customers and revenues.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">We provide services to customers over access lines.&#160; If access lines continue to decline, our operating results may be adversely affected.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Telephone segment generates revenues by delivering voice and data services over access lines.&#160; We continue to experience access </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13<a name="PB_13_082346_7056"></a></font></p>
