<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 8:&#160; ORANGE COUNTY-POUGHKEEPSIE LIMITED PARTNERSHIP</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company was a limited partner in the Orange County-Poughkeepsie Limited Partnership (&#147;O-P&#148;) and had an 8.108% limited partnership interest in the O-P until April&nbsp;30, 2014, which was accounted for under the equity method of accounting.&nbsp; The majority owner and general partner of the O-P is Verizon Wireless of the East LP (&#147;Verizon&#148;).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;26, 2011, the Company entered into an agreement (the &#147;4G Agreement&#148;) with Verizon and Cellco Partnership (d/b/a Verizon Wireless), the other limited partner, in the O-P to make certain changes to the O-P partnership agreement.&nbsp;The 4G Agreement provides that the O-P&#146;s business will be converted from a wholesale business to a retail business.&nbsp;In addition, the 4G Agreement provided for guaranteed annual cash distributions to the Company from the O-P through 2013.&nbsp;For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, the Company received annual cash distributions from the O-P of $13.0 million.&nbsp;The 4G Agreement provided that, starting in 2014, the Company would receive cash distributions equal to its ownership share percentage of the approved total distributions by the O-P. The 4G Agreement also gave the Company the right (the &#147;Put&#148;) to require Verizon to purchase all of the Company&#146;s ownership interest in the O-P during April&nbsp;2013 or April&nbsp;2014 for an amount equal to the greater of (a)&nbsp;$50.0 million or (b)&nbsp;the product of five (5)&nbsp;times 0.081081 times the O-P&#146;s EBITDA, as defined in the 4G Agreement for the calendar year preceding the exercise of the Put.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;30, 2014, the Company exercised the Put option and sold all of its ownership interest in the O-P for gross proceeds of $50 million, which resulted in a gain on the sale of $49.8 million.&#160; The Company will not receive any income from the O-P after April&nbsp;30, 2014.&#160; The Company used a portion of the proceeds to repay all of the outstanding borrowings under the TriState credit facility and paid taxes on the related gain (see Note 10).&#160; The Company expects to use the remaining gross proceeds, among other things, to fund working capital needs and support growth initiatives. The Company may, in its discretion, use the gross proceeds for other purposes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to the equity method accounting of the Company&#146;s investment income, the Company is required to record the income from the O-P as an increase to the Company&#146;s investment account.&nbsp; The Company is required to apply the cash payments made under the 4G Agreement as a return on its investment when received.&nbsp;&nbsp; As a result of receiving the fixed guaranteed cash distributions from the O-P in excess of the Company&#146;s proportionate share of the O-P income, the investment account was reduced to zero during 2012. Thereafter, the Company recorded the fixed guaranteed cash distributions that were received from the O-P in excess of the proportionate share of the O-P income directly to the Company&#146;s statement of operations as other income.&#160; In 2014 when guaranteed distribution ceased, the Company returned to recording the income from the O-P as in increase to the Company&#146;s investment account and any cash payments received were applied as a return on its investment.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, the investment account was zero.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the four months ended April&nbsp;30, 2014, the Company had $2.6 million in income from the O-P equity investment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following summarizes the income statement for the six months ended June&nbsp;30, 2014 and the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 that the O-P provided to the Company:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;11, 2013, the Company entered into a credit agreement with TriState Capital Bank (&#147;TriState&#148;) to provide for borrowings up to $17.0 million (the &#147;Credit Agreement&#148;).&nbsp; The TriState borrowings bore interest at a variable rate based on either LIBOR or a Base Rate, as defined in the Credit Agreement, plus an applicable margin of 3.50% or 2.00%, respectively.&#160;&#160; All borrowings were to become due and payable on June&nbsp;30, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the terms of the Credit Agreement, the Company was required to comply with certain loan covenants, which included, but were not limited to, the achievement of certain financial ratios and certain financial reporting requirements. The Company was required to maintain a consolidated liquidity ratio, as defined in the Credit Agreement, in excess of 1.0 to 1.0.&nbsp; The Company was required to obtain the consent of TriState prior to agreeing to any amendment to agreements between the Company and the O-P. The Company&#146;s obligations under the Credit Agreement were secured by all of the Company&#146;s assets and guaranteed by all of the Company&#146;s wholly-owned subsidiaries except for the Company&#146;s ILEC subsidiary.&nbsp; The ILEC subsidiary entered into a negative pledge agreement with TriState whereby the ILEC subsidiary agreed not to pledge any of its assets as collateral or lien to be placed on any of its assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;30, 2014, the Company sold its ownership interest in the O-P (see Note 8) and a portion of the proceeds was used to repay all of the outstanding borrowings under the Credit Agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June&nbsp;1, 2014, the Company reduced the borrowing capacity under the Credit Agreement from a ceiling of $17.0 million to a ceiling of $5.0 million.&#160; On June&nbsp;30, 2014, the Credit Agreement was amended to extend the expiration of the Credit Agreement from June&nbsp;30, 2014 to October&nbsp;8, 2014.&#160; The Company&#146;s Credit Agreement expired on October&nbsp;8, 2014.&#160; On November&nbsp;7, 2014, the Company entered into a demand line of credit with TriState (the &#147;Demand Line of Credit&#148;) to allow for borrowings up to $5.0 million. The Company borrows or repays its debt as needed based upon its working capital obligations.&#160; It is up to the discretion of TriState to approve borrowings within the allowed line of credit limit and TriState may, at any time, demand that the Company make payment on an outstanding balance. The Company was previously required to comply with certain loan covenants and restrictions under its prior Credit Agreement.&#160; There are no financial covenants under the&#160; Demand Line of Credit.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company did not have any outstanding balance under the Demand Line of Credit.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 10:&#160; INCOME TAXES</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The federal and state components of the provision for income taxes are presented in the following table:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="87%" style="border-collapse:collapse;margin-left:.45in;width:87.34%;">
<tr>
<td width="65%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:65.64%;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred income taxes arise because of differences in the book and tax basis of certain assets and liabilities and tax credit and operating loss carry forwards.&#160; Deferred income tax assets and liabilities consist of the following:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="94%" style="border-collapse:collapse;margin-left:.45in;width:94.0%;">
<tr>
<td width="68%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:68.1%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>    </td>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Based on a current evaluation of expected future taxable income, the Company determined it is not more-likely-than-not that all deferred tax assets will be realized. Therefore, the Company maintained a valuation allowance against its deferred tax assets as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In assessing the realizability of deferred tax assets, management considers whether it is more-likely-than-not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized. The ultimate realization of deferred tax assets is dependent upon the generation of future taxable income of the appropriate character during the periods in which those temporary differences become deductible and the tax credits and loss carryforwards are available to reduce taxable income. In making its assessment, the Company considered all sources of taxable income including carryback potential, future reversals of existing deferred tax liabilities, prudent and feasible tax planning strategies, and lastly, objectively verifiable projections of future taxable income exclusive of reversing temporary differences and carryforwards.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, the Company concluded that its existing deferred tax liabilities represented a source of taxable income to realize its deferred tax assets, exclusive of the deferred tax liability associated with tax amortizable goodwill.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, projections of future taxable income did not provide an additional source of income in the evaluation of the realization of deferred tax assets.&#160; Carryback potential and prudent and feasible tax planning strategies did not provide a source of taxable income in either 2014 or 2013.&#160; The Company will continue to assess all available evidence during future periods to evaluate the realization of its deferred tax assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, the net increase in the Company&#146;s deferred tax assets related principally to its unfunded postretirement liability and the corresponding increase to the valuation allowance has been recorded within other comprehensive income/(loss).&#160; The Company recorded a charge to income of $0.2 million to increase the valuation allowance on the remaining net deferred tax assets at December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, the net decrease in the Company&#146;s deferred tax assets related principally to its unfunded postretirement liability and the corresponding decrease to the valuation allowance has been recorded within other comprehensive income/(loss).&#160; The Company recorded a charge to income of $0.9 million to increase the valuation allowance on the remaining net deferred tax assets at December&nbsp;31, 2013.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for uncertainty in income taxes requires uncertain tax positions to be classified as non-current income tax liabilities unless they are expected to be paid within one year.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has concluded that there are no uncertain tax positions requiring recognition in its consolidated financial statements as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company recognizes interest accrued related to unrecognized tax benefits in interest expense.&#160; For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, there was no interest expense relating to unrecognized tax benefits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had state net operating loss carry-forwards in the amount of approximately $21.8 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; These losses expire through 2034.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company and its subsidiaries file a U.S. federal consolidated income tax return.&#160; The U.S. federal statute of limitations remains open for the years 2011 and thereafter.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">State income tax returns are generally subject to examination for a period of 3 to 5 years after filing the respective return.&#160; The impact of any federal changes on state returns remains subject to examination by the relevant states for a period of up to one year after formal notification to the states. The Company is currently under audit in the state of New Jersey for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 through December&nbsp;31, 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">eligibility.&#160; The non-management plan was frozen as of May&nbsp;1, 2003 and the management plan was frozen as of March&nbsp;1, 2005.&#160; For an eligible employee, benefits are based on years of service and the average of the employee&#146;s three highest consecutive years&#146; of base compensation for years prior to the date on which the plan was frozen.&#160; The Company&#146;s policy is to fund the minimum required contribution disregarding any credit balance arising from excess amounts contributed in the past.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company sponsors a postretirement medical benefit plan that covers all employees that retire directly from active service on or after age 55 with at least 10 years of service.&#160; The projected unit credit actuarial method was used in determining the cost of future benefits.&#160; Assets of the plan are principally invested in fixed income securities and a money market fund.&#160; The Company uses an annual measurement date of December&nbsp;31 for all of its benefit plans.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The rate of return assumption, currently 1.5% for postretirement benefit and 7% for pension benefits, estimates the portion of plan benefits that will be derived from investment return and the portion that will come directly from Company contributions.&#160; Accordingly, the Company strives to maintain an investment portfolio that generates annual returns from funds invested consistent with achieving the projected long-term rate of return required for plan assets.&#160; The decrease in the expected rate of return on plan assets for the postretirement benefit plans was due to a change in the investment strategy based on the expected utilization of plan assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The projected pension benefit obligation of $21.2 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 was in excess of plan assets of $13.2 million, leading to an unfunded projected benefit obligation of $8.1 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; The projected benefit obligation of $18.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 was in excess of plan assets of $13.1 million, leading to an unfunded projected benefit obligation of $5.4 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2013. The projected pension benefit obligation exceeded the fair value of plan assets at December&nbsp;31, 2014, and the projected benefit obligation increased from the same period December&nbsp;31, 2013. The Company was required to record an increase to its pension liability on its Consolidated Balance Sheet as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, and the effect of this adjustment was an increase in the pension liability of $2.7 million and an increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss of $2.5 million. The increase in the projected benefit obligation was primarily attributable to a decrease in the discount rate and the adoption of new mortality tables.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s postretirement plans had an unfunded projected benefit obligation of $0.8 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; The projected benefit obligation of $2.9 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 was in excess of plan assets of $2.1 million.&#160; The Company&#146;s postretirement plans had a benefit obligation of $2.8 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The health care cost trend rates (representing the assumed annual percentage increase in claim costs by year) was 7.5% for the year 2014 grading down to 5% in 2021 and later by 0.5% per year.&#160; The Company&#146;s most recent actuarial calculation anticipates that this trend will continue into 2015.&#160; An increase in the assumed health care cost trend rate by 1.0% would increase the accumulated postretirement benefit obligation as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 by approximately $0.3 million.&#160; A 1.0% decrease in the health care cost trend rate would decrease these components by $0.2 million. The projected postretirement benefit obligation exceeded the fair value of plan assets at December&nbsp;31, 2014, and the projected benefit obligation increased from the same period December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The Company was required to record an increase to its postretirement liability on its Consolidated Balance Sheet as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and the effect of this adjustment was an increase in the postretirement liability of $0.1 million and an decrease in accumulated other comprehensive income of $0.1 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;8, 2003, the Medicare Prescription Drug Improvement Modernization Act of 2003 (the &#147;Act&#148;) was signed into law.&nbsp;The Act introduces a prescription drug benefit under Medicare Part&nbsp;D, as well as a federal subsidy to sponsors of retiree health care benefit plans that provide benefits at least actuarially equivalent to Medicare Part&nbsp;D. The Company has not applied for a subsidy as it has not done an assessment to determine if it is actuarially equivalent to Medicare Part&nbsp;D under the Act. Therefore, a subsidy is not included in the actuarial assumptions for its postretirement benefits plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Plan Assets</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company diversifies its pension and postretirement plan assets across domestic and international common stock and fixed income asset classes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the current target allocations for pension and postretirement plan assets are 50-60% for equity securities, 40-50% for fixed income securities and 0-10% for cash and certain other investments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Equity securities and fixed income securities categorized as Level&nbsp;1 represent mutual funds that are traded on national and international exchanges and are valued at their closing prices on the last trading day of the year. Additionally, some equity securities and fixed income securities are public investment vehicles valued using the Net Asset Value (&#147;NAV&#148;) provided by the fund manager. The NAV is the total value of the fund divided by the number of shares outstanding.&#160;&#160; As the underlying securities to these funds are nationally traded and these funds do not have redemption restrictions, they are categorized as Level 2.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with its contribution policy, in 2015 the Company expects to make the required contribution of $0.2 million to its pension plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company also has a defined contribution 401(k)&nbsp;Profit Sharing Plan covering certain eligible employees. Under the plan, employees may contribute up to 100% of compensation not to exceed certain legal limitations.&#160; The Company matches 100% of the participant&#146;s contributions, up to either 4.0% or 4.5% of compensation, as set forth in the plan.&#160; The Company contributed and expensed $0.4 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 12:&#160; STOCK BASED COMPENSATION</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.2pt;text-indent:-1.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a shareholder approved long-term incentive plan (the &#147;LTIP&#148;) to assist the Company and its affiliates in attracting, motivating and retaining selected individuals to serve as employees, directors, consultants and advisors of the Company and its affiliates by providing incentives to such individuals through the ownership and performance of the Company&#146;s common stock. There are 1.1 million shares of common stock authorized for issuance under the LTIP.&#160; Shares available for grant under the LTIP may be either authorized, but unissued shares or shares that have been reacquired by the Company and designated as treasury shares. As of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and December&nbsp;31, 2013, 420,392 and 57,923 shares, respectively, of the Company&#146;s common stock were available for grant under the LTIP. The LTIP permits the issuance by the Company of awards in the form of stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock and restricted stock units and performance shares. The exercise price per share of the Company&#146;s common stock purchasable under any stock option or stock appreciation right may not be less than 100% of the fair market value of one share of common stock on the date of grant. The term of any stock option or stock appreciation right may not exceed ten years. The LTIP also provides plan participants with a cashless mechanism to exercise their stock options. Issued restricted stock, stock options and restricted stock units are subject to vesting restrictions.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.2pt;text-indent:-1.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, $0.7 million of total unrecognized compensation expense related to stock options and restricted stock is expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of approximately 1.74 years.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Shareholder Rights Plan</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;2, 2014, in connection with an unsolicited, non-binding acquisition proposal, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors (the &#147;Alteva Board&#148;) adopted a Stockholder Rights Plan that provides for the distribution of one right for each share of common stock outstanding.&#160; Each right entitles the holder to purchase one one-thousandth (1/1000</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">) of a share of Series&nbsp;A Junior Participating Preferred Stock, par value of $0.01 per share, of the Company (the &#147;Preferred Stock&#148;) at a price of $22.20 per one-thousandth of a share of Preferred Stock, subject to adjustment.&#160; The rights generally become distributed and exercisable at the discretion of the Alteva Board following a public announcement that 20% or more of the Company&#146;s common stock has been acquired or an intent to acquire has become apparent.&#160; The rights will expire on September&nbsp;1, 2015, unless the final expiration date is advanced or extended or unless the rights are earlier redeemed or exchanged by the Company.&#160; Further description and terms of the rights are set forth in the Rights Agreement between the Company and American Stock Transfer&nbsp;&amp; Trust Company, LLC.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company is not aware of the occurrence of any events that would trigger the rights under the plan.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Share Repurchase Program</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;25, 2014, the Alteva Board authorized a repurchase program for up to $3.0 million of its common stock.&#160; Share purchases may take place in open market transactions or in privately negotiated transaction and may be made from time to time depending on market conditions, share price, trading volume and other factors. The repurchase program authorized by the Alteva Board does not require the Company to acquire a specific number of shares, and may be terminated, suspended, or modified at any time. The timing and actual number of shares repurchased, if any, will depend on a variety of factors including the market price of the Company&#146;s common stock, regulatory, legal and contractual requirements, and other market factors.&nbsp;The share repurchase is expected to be funded from available cash on hand.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company repurchased 9,600 shares under the repurchase program at a value of $0.1 million.&#160; Shares were purchased on the open market at the prevailing days&#146; stock price, plus transaction costs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 13:&#160; EARNINGS (LOSS) PER SHARE</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Basic earnings (loss) per share is computed by dividing net income (loss) applicable to common stock by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding during the period.&nbsp; Diluted earnings (loss) per share is computed by dividing net income (loss) applicable to common stock by the weighted average number of shares of common stock adjusted to include the effect of potentially dilutive securities.&nbsp; Potentially dilutive securities include incremental shares issuable upon exercise of outstanding stock options and shares of unvested restricted stock.&nbsp; Diluted earnings (loss) per share excludes all dilutive securities if their effect is anti-dilutive.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s restricted stock awards are considered &#147;participating securities&#148; because they contain non-forfeitable rights to dividends. Under the two-class method, earnings per share (&#147;EPS&#148;) is computed by dividing earnings allocated to common shareholders by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding for the period. In applying the two-class method, earnings are allocated to both shares of common stock and participating securities based on their respective weighted-average shares outstanding for the period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, the Company experienced a net loss.&nbsp; As a result, the effect of participating securities was excluded from the computation of basic and diluted EPS.&nbsp; The net losses were not allocated because the restricted stockholders are not required to fund losses.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The weighted average number of shares of common stock used in basic and diluted earnings per share for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, were as follows:</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 15:&#160; SEGMENT INFORMATION</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s two segments, UC and Telephone, are strategic business units that offer different products and services.&nbsp; The Company evaluates the performance of its two segments based upon factors such as revenue growth, expense containment, market share and operating results.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The UC segment is a premier provider of hosted Unified Communications as a Service (&#147;UCaaS&#148;) including VoIP, hosted Microsoft communication services, fixed mobile convergence and advanced voice applications for a broad customer base including, medium and large-sized businesses and enterprise business customers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Telephone segment operates as an ILEC in southern Orange County, New York and northern New Jersey.&#160; The Telephone segment consists of providing local and toll telephone service, high-speed broadband and fiber Internet access services and satellite video services to residential and business customers.&#160; The ILEC service areas are primarily rural and have an estimated population of 50,000.&#160; The Company also operates as a CLEC in in Middletown, New York, Scotchtown, New York and Vernon, New Jersey.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The segment results presented below are not necessarily indicative of the results of operations these segments would have achieved had they operated as stand-alone entities during the periods presented.&#160; All intersegment transactions are shown net of eliminations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 17:&#160; COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is party, from time to time, to various legal proceedings, including patent infringement claims, regulatory investigations and tax examinations incidental to its business.&#160; The Company continually monitors these legal proceedings, regulatory investigations and tax examinations to determine the impact and any required accruals.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;31, 2014, David J. Cuthbert was terminated as President and Chief Executive Officer of Alteva.&#160; The Company notified Mr.&nbsp;Cuthbert that his termination was for &#147;cause&#148; and, as such, Mr.&nbsp;Cuthbert was not entitled to any of the benefits provided for under his employment agreement dated March&nbsp;5, 2013, including cash severance and the acceleration of vesting on any unvested equity instruments.&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Cuthbert disputed the Company&#146;s basis for termination and claimed that he was due his full severance benefits.</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As the Company did not want to incur further legal fees or the risk of distraction of a protracted legal dispute, on October&nbsp;16, 2014, the Company, through mediation, entered into a settlement agreement and mutual release agreement (the &#147;Settlement Agreement&#148;) with Mr.&nbsp;Cuthbert.&nbsp;&nbsp;In consideration for Mr.&nbsp;Cuthbert&#146;s execution of the Settlement Agreement, the Company agreed to pay to Mr.&nbsp;Cuthbert the amount of $0.75 million less certain taxes and withholdings, which was paid out on October&nbsp;28, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total expense, net of insurance recoveries, of $0.7 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 is included in the loss on disposal, restructuring costs and other special charges line in the condensed statement of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company was named as a party to a lawsuit from Sprint regarding a certain tariff charge (IntraMTA carrier charge) billed by Alteva, paid by Sprint over a number of years that had not previously been disputed. Sprint has filed similar lawsuits against other carriers related to the same tariff charges. The Company has filed a motion to dismiss.&#160; The amount of the claim filed by Sprint is for $0.2 million; however the Company has not been able to substantiate the basis for the claim amount and therefore, has not recorded an accrual as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company leases office equipment for operations as well as office space in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.&#160; Total expenses associated with these agreements were $0.4 million and $0.5 million in 2014 and 2013, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In February&nbsp;2015, the Company entered into an agreement to terminate the lease for its corporate headquarters in Philadelphia, PA.&#160; As part of the agreement to terminate the lease, the Company will receive a payment of either $1.5 million or $1.25 million, depending upon the date the Company vacates the facility.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company had leasehold improvements and furniture and fixtures with a net book value of $0.7 million and deferred rent of $0.4 million recognized in the balance sheet related to this leased facility. &#160;In connection with the lease termination, the Company entered into a lease for a new corporate headquarters in Philadelphia, PA in February&nbsp;2015.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 9.&#160; <i>CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH <a name="Item9_ChangesInAndDisagreementsWi_101246"></a>ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE.</i></font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This item is not applicable.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 9A.<i>&#160; CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES.</i></font></b><a name="Item9a_ControlsAndProcedures__101254"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Background</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;14, 2014, management and the Audit Committee of our Board of Directors (the &#147;Audit Committee&#148;), determined that, due to an error in the application of U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#147;GAAP&#148;) for income taxes related to the determination of the valuation allowance needed to reflect its deferred tax assets at the amount that is more than likely than not realizable, our previously filed consolidated financial statements and related financial statement schedules as of and for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, contained in our Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K/A for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, should be restated.&nbsp; This conclusion was reached because the Company determined that it overstated its prepaid income taxes and deferred income taxes in the consolidated balance sheet at December&nbsp;31, 2012 by $0.3 million and $1.1 million, respectively, due to the need to increase its valuation allowance, which resulted in an understatement of the net loss reported for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 by $1.4 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, the Audit Committee concluded that, due to similar errors in income tax accounting, the condensed interim financial statements as of March&nbsp;31, 2013, June&nbsp;30, 2013 and September&nbsp;30, 2013 included in our Quarterly Reports on Forms 10-Q for the respective fiscal quarters then ended should be restated.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We maintain disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and 15d-15(e)&nbsp;of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#147;Exchange Act&#148;), that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in our Exchange Act reports are recorded, processed, summarized, and reported within the time periods specified in rules&nbsp;and forms of the Securities and Exchange Commission, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosures.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, our management carried out an assessment under the supervision of and with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures pursuant to Exchange Act Rules&nbsp;13a-15(b)&nbsp;and 15d-15(b).&#160; As a result of this assessment, the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and that the material weakness described in &#147;Remediation of Prior Material Weaknesses in Internal Control over Financial Reporting&#148; below had been remediated.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Remediation of Prior Material Weaknesses in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As previously disclosed, we identified a material weakness as of December&nbsp;31, 2013, specifically related to accounting for the valuation allowance for deferred income tax assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In response to the identified material weakness, our management, with oversight from our Audit Committee, implemented a plan of remediation.&#160; The remediation plan was developed following an investigation and review of the processes and activities surrounding the material weakness and included changes to these processes to prevent or detect similar future occurrences.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of the plan, we executed the following control improvements during 2014:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We added additional reviews and worked with our internal and external resources to enhance our process and controls around the evaluation, review and reporting of our taxes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We changed our external tax provider.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has completed the documentation and testing of the corrective actions described above and, as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, has concluded that the remediation activities implemented are sufficient to allow us to conclude that the previously disclosed material weakness has been remediated as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">56<a name="PB_56_101335_7748"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Management&#146;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;and 15d-15(f)&nbsp;under the Exchange Act.&#160; Our internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external reporting purposes in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.&#160; Internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (i)&nbsp;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of our assets; (ii)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that our receipts and expenditures are being made only in accordance with authorizations of our management and directors; and (iii)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of our assets that could have a material effect on the interim or annual consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A material weakness is a deficiency, or a combination of deficiencies, in internal control over financial reporting, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of a company&#146;s annual or interim financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, based on the criteria described in the <i>Internal Control-Integrated Framework </i>issued in 2013 by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&#160; Based on this assessment, our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rule&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;and 15d-15(f)&nbsp;under the Exchange Act) during the fourth quarter of our fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
